# AeroZoo {#sec-aerozoo}

```{python}
#| label: setup-aerozoo
#| include: false
import json, math, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
RES = Path("..") / "results"
AZ = RES / "campaigns_2026-10-09" / "aerozoo"
R = json.load(open(AZ / "aerozoo_reduction.json"))
LAB = json.load(open(AZ / "case_labels.json")); LAB_META = LAB.pop("_meta")
mean = statistics.mean
FIELDS = list(R["fields"].items())            # [(metric key, label)] in the book's order
FKEYS = [k for k, _ in FIELDS]
FLAB = dict(FIELDS)
SPLITS = R["splits"]
ARMS = [a for a in ("ISLA", "ISLA-DTT", "GeoTransolver") if a in R["arms"]]
BASELINES = [a for a in ARMS if a != "ISLA"]
KEY = {"ISLA": "isla_ref", "ISLA-DTT": "isla_dtt", "GeoTransolver": "gt", "ISLA (half rate)": "isla_hr", "ISLA-DTT (half rate)": "isla_dtt_hr"}
CONFIG = {"ISLA": "ISLA width 512 with 512 slices, 12 layers, cosine routing, learning rate 3.75e-4",
          "ISLA-DTT": "ISLA-DTT, the same configuration with the read-only tree read (a Barnes-Hut forest at theta 1, built in a frame the boundary carries) in place of the interacting prediction points",
          "GeoTransolver": "GeoTransolver width 256 with 256 slices, 12 layers, learning rate 1e-3",
          "ISLA (half rate)": "the ISLA reference configuration at 1.875e-4, half the rate 3.75e-4 at which it trains on every dataset, as a labeled rate control",
          "ISLA-DTT (half rate)": "ISLA-DTT at the same half rate"}
# the half-rate arms (a labeled rate control) appear where they have trained; the standing tables stay with the reference-rate arms
HR_ARMS = [a for a in ("ISLA (half rate)", "ISLA-DTT (half rate)") if any(m["arm"] == a for m in R["runs"].values())]
BVR = R.get("bestval", {})           # best-checkpoint diagnostic: BVR[arm][split][side]
EV = R.get("events", {})             # the instability detector per lane
have = lambda arm, split, side: side in R["arms"].get(arm, {}).get(split, {})
blk = lambda arm, split, side: R["arms"][arm][split][side]
err = lambda arm, split, side, f: blk(arm, split, side)["fields"][f]["mean"]
seeds = lambda arm, split, side, f: list(blk(arm, split, side)["fields"][f]["per_seed"].values())
rat = lambda arm, split, side, f: R["ratios"][split][side][arm][f]
lead = lambda r: f"{(r - 1) * 100:.0f}%"
trail = lambda r: f"{(1 - r) * 100:.0f}%"
def fmt_ratio(r):
    """A ratio as the book writes it: two decimals near one, one decimal to ten, none above."""
    return f"{r:.0f}x" if r >= 10 else f"{r:.1f}x" if r >= 2 else f"{r:.2f}"
def standing(r, b_seeds, i_seeds):
    """Word a baseline ÷ ISLA ratio: a lead or a deficit when every baseline seed sits on one side of every ISLA seed, level when the seeds interleave."""
    if min(b_seeds) > max(i_seeds): return f"leads by {r:.2f}x" if r >= 1.5 else f"leads by {lead(r)}"
    if max(b_seeds) < min(i_seeds): return f"trails by {trail(r)}"
    return f"is level (ratio {r:.2f})"
word = lambda arm, split, side, f: standing(rat(arm, split, side, f)["mean_ratio"], seeds(arm, split, side, f), seeds("ISLA", split, side, f))
# the headline side: the sealed test side once it is scored for ISLA and GeoTransolver, the validation side until then
SIDE = "test" if have("ISLA", "full", "test") and have("GeoTransolver", "full", "test") else "val"
SIDE_WORD = {"test": "the sealed test side", "val": "the validation side"}[SIDE]
N_HEAD = blk("ISLA", "full", SIDE)["fields"][FKEYS[0]]["n_cases"]
N_SEEDS = blk("ISLA", "full", SIDE)["fields"][FKEYS[0]]["n_seeds"]
HELD = [s for s in ("family_non_box", "reynolds", "bank_blobs") if s in R["penalties"] and "ISLA" in R["penalties"][s] and "GeoTransolver" in R["penalties"][s]]
HELD_WORD = {"family_non_box": "the enclosure family", "reynolds": "the Reynolds range", "bank_blobs": "the blob bank"}
pen = lambda arm, split, f: R["penalties"][split][arm][f]["mean_ratio"]
# cost: the full-split lanes, seed means
def cost_of(arm, split="full"):
    rows = [c for c in R["cost"].get(arm, {}).get(split, {}).values() if c.get("step_seconds_median")]
    if not rows: return None
    return {"step_s": mean(c["step_seconds_median"] for c in rows), "mem_gb": max(c["mem_gb_max"] for c in rows if c.get("mem_gb_max")),
            "params": next((c["n_parameters"] for c in rows if c.get("n_parameters")), None),
            "gpu_h": mean(c["gpu_hours_est"] for c in rows if c.get("gpu_hours_est")) if any(c.get("gpu_hours_est") for c in rows) else None,
            "steps_per_epoch": rows[0].get("steps_per_epoch"), "trained": all(c.get("trained") for c in rows)}
COST = {a: cost_of(a) for a in ARMS}
PARAMS = {a: (COST[a]["params"] / 1e6 if COST[a] and COST[a]["params"] else float("nan")) for a in ARMS}
# figure helpers shared with the other dataset chapters
PF = RES / "problem_figures_2026-09-22"
SF = RES / "sample_figures_2026-10-02"
def load_problem(name):
    """One representative sample of a dataset, reduced for plotting (results/problem_figures_2026-09-22/)."""
    z = np.load(PF / f"{name}.npz"); meta = json.load(open(PF / f"{name}.json"))
    return {k: z[k] for k in z.files}, meta
def load_samples(name):
    """Several samples of a dataset, reduced for plotting (results/sample_figures_2026-10-02/); per-sample arrays are
    concatenated and cut with the matching ``*_offsets`` array via ``part``."""
    z = np.load(SF / f"{name}.npz"); meta = json.load(open(SF / f"{name}.json"))
    return {k: z[k] for k in z.files}, meta
def part(a, off, i):
    """Rows of the concatenated array ``a`` that belong to sample ``i``."""
    return a[off[i]:off[i + 1]]
def field_scatter(ax, xy, v, s=3.0, signed=False, vmin=None, vmax=None):
    if signed:
        lim = max(abs(np.nanmin(v)), abs(np.nanmax(v))) if vmin is None else None
        norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.0, vmin=(-lim if vmin is None else vmin), vmax=(lim if vmax is None else vmax))
        return ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=v, s=s, lw=0, cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm, rasterized=True)
    return ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=v, s=s, lw=0, cmap=SEQUENTIAL, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, rasterized=True)
def small_colorbar(fig, sc, ax, label, **kw):
    cb = fig.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, fraction=0.035, pad=0.02, **kw); cb.outline.set_visible(False); cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=8)
    cb.set_label(label, fontsize=8.5)
    return cb
def seed_marks(ax, x, vals, color, w=0.18):
    """Seeds as short horizontal ticks at x; the seed mean is the series mark."""
    for v in vals:
        ax.plot([x - w, x + w], [v, v], color=color, lw=1.1, solid_capstyle="butt", zorder=4)
# ---- AeroZoo figure helpers: the reduced arrays are in the stored (world) frame; ``frame`` (rows: inlet direction, in-plane
# cross-flow axis, plane normal) about ``body_centroid`` projects them into the mid-span plane ----
AZ_WALL = {0: ("inlet", "value"), 1: ("outlet", "flux"), 2: ("no-slip wall", "value"), 3: ("slip wall / symmetry plane", "free")}
AZ_BODY = {0: ("body, no-slip band", "value"), 1: ("body, slip band", "free")}
AZ_ENCLOSURE = {"external_box": "box", "external_opposed_hemisphere": "spherical cap on a symmetry plane",
                "external_opposed_sphere": "sphere, inlet and outlet halves", "internal_duct": "duct"}
AZ_SHORT = {"external_box": "box", "external_opposed_hemisphere": "spherical cap", "external_opposed_sphere": "sphere", "internal_duct": "duct"}
AZ_PROFILE = {"opposed_hemisphere_symmetry": "", "opposed_hemispheres": ""}   # scenario names that only repeat the enclosure family
SLIP_FACE = "#d9d8d0"   # the slip band on a solid body rendering (the lug figure's tint for "free")
def in_plane(p, frame, c):
    """Plane-frame coordinates (x1 along the inlet flow, x2 across it in the plane, d normal to the plane) of world points."""
    return (np.asarray(p, np.float64) - np.asarray(c, np.float64)) @ np.asarray(frame, np.float64).T
def sized_scatter(ax, xy, size_m, c, span_m, k=1.5, smin=0.4, smax=80.0, **kw):
    """Scatter cells as squares whose side follows the cell size, so a slice of a graded mesh reads as a filled field."""
    pts_per_m = ax.get_position().width * ax.figure.get_figwidth() * 72 / span_m
    s = np.clip((k * np.asarray(size_m) * pts_per_m) ** 2, smin, smax)
    return ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=c, s=s, lw=0, marker="s", rasterized=True, **kw)
def cut(q, size, k=0.75):
    """Rows of plane-frame points ``q`` whose cell the plane passes through (|d| within k cell sizes)."""
    return np.abs(q[:, 2]) <= k * np.asarray(size)
# stratified blocks on the headline side (by_quality / by_label come with the test side and with every full-split side)
def strata(arm, kind, split="full", side=None):
    b = blk(arm, split, side or SIDE)
    return b["by_quality"] if kind == "quality" else b["by_label"][kind]
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Trained with the raw slice reads"}
The trained checkpoints behind this chapter's numbers and pictures use the raw slice reads, in which the slice sublayer pools and broadcasts the raw token state rather than its LayerNorm, not the normalized reads of ISLA's reference configuration (@sec-isla-layer).
:::

## The problem: bodies from seven banks in four enclosures across five Reynolds decades {#sec-dataset-aerozoo}

**AeroZoo v1.2 is 3,816 time-averaged solutions of the incompressible Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes equations with the transition SST closure, each around a different body placed in its own enclosure at its own size and Reynolds number.** The body comes from one of seven geometry banks (procedural blobs, cars, streamlined bodies, airframes, two Blender banks of bluff and streamlined shapes, and a CAD bank), the enclosure is an external box under one of five boundary-condition profiles, a pair of opposed hemispheres or opposed spheres, or an internal duct, and the Reynolds number is drawn across five decades from $10^3$ to $10^8$. A body's surface is all no-slip or carries slip bands. Every case is handed to the model as the boundary-value problem that produced it: four boundary meshes keyed by the kind of condition they carry (`inlet`, `outlet`, `no_slip`, `slip`), each face with its prescribed values, and the global data that close the problem (the inlet direction, the Reynolds number, the inlet turbulence). The interior is a cloud of 0.6 to 24 million cell centroids (median 5 million) carrying velocity, gauge pressure, turbulent viscosity, turbulent kinetic energy and the specific dissipation rate; the model predicts the five at 200,000 of them per case. @fig-aerozoo-problem shows one validation case.

```{python}
#| label: fig-aerozoo-problem
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The AeroZoo problem, on one validation case: a procedural car inside a
#|   spherical cap that stands on a symmetry plane. Top: the boundaries the
#|   model is handed, each cell drawn where the mid-span plane cuts it and
#|   colored by the kind of condition it carries: the inlet dome prescribes
#|   the velocity and the turbulence quantities (value), the outlet dome the
#|   gauge pressure, zero, with zero normal gradient on the velocity (flux),
#|   the symmetry plane and the body's slip band carry a slip condition
#|   (free), and the body's no-slip band carries $u = 0$ (value). The black
#|   arrow is the inlet direction, the one global vector; the box lists this
#|   case's global scalars. Middle left: the body alone, its two bands.
#|   Middle right: the pressure coefficient $C_p = p / q_\mathrm{ref}$ at the
#|   interior cells the plane cuts, within two reference lengths of the body,
#|   each cell drawn at its own size with the body's section outlined.
#|   Bottom: the same $C_p$ and the speed ratio $|U| / U_\mathrm{ref}$ over
#|   the whole plane, two of the task's five targets. The plane is built
#|   from the data (through the body's centroid, containing the inlet
#|   direction, normal to the body's widest cross-flow axis), so $x_1$ runs
#|   along the inlet flow and $x_2$ across it; the stored coordinates are a
#|   random rotation of this view, and the stored inlet direction is printed
#|   in the box. How to read this: colors are the reference CFD fields, not
#|   predictions; the body's surface is split into a no-slip and a slip band
#|   by the generator, so the slip color on the body is a condition, not a
#|   rendering choice; the body is off the enclosure's axis because bodies
#|   are placed at random inside their enclosures; what the figure does not
#|   show is the enclosure's third dimension, the inlet and outlet are domes
#|   and the symmetry plane a disk. Data:
#|   results/problem_figures_2026-09-22/aerozoo.npz.
#| code-fold: true
from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d.art3d import Poly3DCollection
from matplotlib.colors import to_rgba_array
A, Am = load_problem("aerozoo")
F, c0 = A["frame"], A["body_centroid"]
S = in_plane(A["slice_points"], F, c0); B = in_plane(A["body_points"], F, c0); W = in_plane(A["band_points"], F, c0)
L = Am["L_ref"]; bm = cut(B, A["body_size"])
x1lim = (W[:, 0].min() - 0.03 * L, W[:, 0].max() + 0.03 * L); x2lim = (W[:, 1].min() - 0.03 * L, W[:, 1].max() + 0.03 * L)
span = x1lim[1] - x1lim[0]; h = x2lim[1] - x2lim[0]
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.0, vmin=-1.0, vmax=1.0)
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(8, 11.0))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 2, height_ratios=[1.75, 1.15, 1.0], hspace=0.42, wspace=0.12)
gsb = gs[2, :].subgridspec(1, 2, wspace=0.45)
# -- top: the boundaries by condition, in the mid-span plane
ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :])
for r, (lab, kind) in AZ_WALL.items():
    m = A["band_role"] == r
    if m.any():
        sized_scatter(ax, W[m, :2], A["band_size"][m], BC[kind], span, k=2.4, smin=5.0, zorder=3)
for r, (lab, kind) in AZ_BODY.items():
    m = bm & (A["body_role"] == r)
    sized_scatter(ax, B[m, :2], A["body_size"][m], BC[kind], span, k=2.4, smin=5.0, zorder=4)
map_axes(ax); ax.set_xlim(*x1lim); ax.set_ylim(*x2lim)
ax.set_ylabel("$x_2$, across the flow in the plane [m]"); ax.set_xlabel("$x_1$, along the inlet flow from the body centroid [m]")
ax.set_title("the boundaries, where the mid-span plane cuts them: inlet and outlet domes, symmetry plane, the body's two bands", fontsize=9.5)
xa, ya = x1lim[0] + 0.14 * span, x2lim[0] + 0.72 * h
ax.annotate("", xy=(xa + 0.1 * span, ya), xytext=(xa, ya), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=INK, lw=2.0), zorder=6)
ax.text(xa + 0.11 * span, ya, f"inlet flow $\\hat g_1$ (the global vector), $U_\\mathrm{{ref}}$ = {Am['U_ref']:.2f} m/s", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=8.2, color=INK2)
ax.text(x1lim[0] + 0.08 * span, x2lim[0] + 0.5 * h, "inlet dome: velocity, $k$, $\\omega$,\n$\\gamma$, $Re_\\theta$ prescribed (value)", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=7.8, color=BC["value"], path_effects=halo())
ax.text(x1lim[1] - 0.1 * span, x2lim[0] + 0.5 * h, "outlet dome: $p$ = 0,\n$\\partial u / \\partial n$ = 0 (flux)", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=7.8, color=BC["flux"], path_effects=halo())
ax.text(0.5 * (x1lim[0] + x1lim[1]), x2lim[0] + 0.035 * h, "symmetry plane: slip (free)", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.8, color=BC["free"], path_effects=halo())
ax.text(B[bm, 0].max() + 0.02 * span, B[bm, 1].min(), "the body: a no-slip band, $u$ = 0 (value),\nand a slip band (free)", ha="left", va="top", fontsize=7.8, color=BC["value"], path_effects=halo())
nb = Am["n_boundary_cells_by_role"]
ax.text(x1lim[0] + 0.08 * span, x2lim[0] + 0.3 * h,
        f"global scalars: $U_\\mathrm{{ref}}$ = {Am['U_ref']:.2f} m/s, $L_\\mathrm{{ref}}$ = {L:.3f} m, $\\nu$ = {Am['nu']:.2e} m²/s, $\\rho$ = {Am['rho']:.3f} kg/m³\n"
        f"Re = $U_\\mathrm{{ref}} L_\\mathrm{{ref}} / \\nu$ = {Am['Re']:.2e}; inlet $k$ = {Am['inlet']['turbulent_kinetic_energy']:.2e} m²/s², $\\omega$ = {Am['inlet']['specific_dissipation_rate']:.3g} 1/s\n"
        f"boundary cells {Am['n_boundary_cells']:,} (inlet {nb['inlet']:,}, outlet {nb['outlet']:,}, no-slip {nb['no_slip']:,}, slip {nb['slip']:,}); volume cells {Am['n_interior_points']:,}\n"
        f"stored frame: inlet direction ({', '.join(f'{v:.2f}' for v in np.asarray(Am['U_inf']) / Am['U_ref'])}), a random rotation of this view",
        ha="left", va="top", fontsize=7.2, color=INK2, linespacing=1.4, bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec=BASELINE))
# -- middle left: the body alone
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0], projection="3d"); ax3.set_proj_type("ortho")
mp = in_plane(A["body_mesh_points"], F, c0)[:, [0, 2, 1]]; tri = mp[A["body_mesh_cells"]]
face = to_rgba_array(np.where(A["body_mesh_role"] == 0, BC["value"], SLIP_FACE))
coll = Poly3DCollection(tri, facecolors=face, shade=True); coll.set_edgecolor("none"); ax3.add_collection3d(coll)
ext = mp.max(0) - mp.min(0)
ax3.set_xlim(mp[:, 0].min(), mp[:, 0].max()); ax3.set_ylim(mp[:, 1].min(), mp[:, 1].max()); ax3.set_zlim(mp[:, 2].min(), mp[:, 2].max())
ax3.set_box_aspect(tuple(ext / ext.max()), zoom=1.5); ax3.view_init(elev=28, azim=-135); ax3.set_axis_off()
ax3.set_title(f"the body: {Am['n_body_cells']:,} surface cells in two bands, from upstream and above", fontsize=9.5, loc="left")
ax3.text2D(0.02, 0.1, "no-slip band: $u$ = 0 (value)", transform=ax3.transAxes, color=BC["value"], fontsize=8.2, path_effects=halo())
ax3.text2D(0.02, 0.03, "slip band (free)", transform=ax3.transAxes, color=BC["free"], fontsize=8.2, path_effects=halo())
# -- middle right: Cp near the body
axz = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
zx = (B[bm, 0].min() - 1.0 * L, B[bm, 0].max() + 2.0 * L); zy = (-1.1 * L, 1.1 * L)
win = (S[:, 0] > zx[0]) & (S[:, 0] < zx[1]) & (S[:, 1] > zy[0]) & (S[:, 1] < zy[1])
sc = sized_scatter(axz, S[win, :2], A["slice_size"][win], A["slice_cp"][win], zx[1] - zx[0], cmap=DIVERGING, norm=norm, zorder=2)
sized_scatter(axz, B[bm, :2], A["body_size"][bm], INK, zx[1] - zx[0], k=1.6, smin=3.0, zorder=4)
map_axes(axz); axz.set_xlim(*zx); axz.set_ylim(*zy); axz.set_xlabel("$x_1$ [m]"); axz.set_ylabel("$x_2$ [m]")
axz.set_title("$C_p$ in the plane, within two $L_\\mathrm{ref}$ of the body", fontsize=9.5)
small_colorbar(fig, sc, axz, "$C_p$ [–]", extend="both")
# -- bottom: the two fields over the whole plane
def field_panel(ax, v, cmap, norm=None, vmin=None, vmax=None, outline=INK):
    sc = sized_scatter(ax, S[:, :2], A["slice_size"], v, span, cmap=cmap, norm=norm, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax, zorder=2)
    sized_scatter(ax, W[:, :2], A["band_size"], BASELINE, span, k=1.6, smin=2.0, zorder=3)
    sized_scatter(ax, B[bm, :2], A["body_size"][bm], outline, span, k=1.6, smin=2.0, zorder=4)
    map_axes(ax); ax.set_xlim(*x1lim); ax.set_ylim(*x2lim); ax.set_xlabel("$x_1$ [m]")
    return sc
ax = fig.add_subplot(gsb[0, 0]); sc = field_panel(ax, A["slice_cp"], DIVERGING, norm=norm); ax.set_ylabel("$x_2$ [m]")
ax.set_title("$C_p = p / q_\\mathrm{ref}$ over the whole plane", fontsize=9.5)
small_colorbar(fig, sc, ax, "$C_p$ [–]", extend="both")
um = A["slice_umag"]; vmax = float(np.ceil(np.quantile(um, 0.995) * 10) / 10)
ax = fig.add_subplot(gsb[0, 1]); sc = field_panel(ax, um, SEQUENTIAL, vmin=0, vmax=vmax, outline=WHITE)
ax.set_title("$|U| / U_\\mathrm{ref}$ over the whole plane", fontsize=9.5)
small_colorbar(fig, sc, ax, "$|U| / U_\\mathrm{ref}$ [–]", extend="max")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
    x1 = (min(S[:, 0].min(), W[:, 0].min()), max(S[:, 0].max(), W[:, 0].max())); x2 = (min(S[:, 1].min(), W[:, 1].min()), max(S[:, 1].max(), W[:, 1].max()))
    pad = 0.03 * (x1[1] - x1[0])
    P.append(dict(S=S, B=B, W=W, x1=(x1[0] - pad, x1[1] + pad), x2=(x2[0] - pad, x2[1] + pad), aspect=(x2[1] - x2[0]) / (x1[1] - x1[0] + 2 * pad),
                  ssz=part(Zs_["slice_size"], so, i), bsz=part(Zs_["body_size"], bo, i), wsz=part(Zs_["band_size"], lo_, i),
                  um=part(Zs_["slice_umag"], so, i), wrole=part(Zs_["band_role"], lo_, i), c=c))

        xa, ya = p["x1"][0] + 0.03 * span, p["x2"][0] + 0.86 * h
        ax.annotate("", xy=(xa + 0.1 * span, ya), xytext=(xa, ya), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=INK, lw=1.6), zorder=6)
```

### Files, conversion and normalization {#sec-data-aerozoo}

**3,816 released cases of AeroZoo v1.2 (Peter Sharpe's generator; release
of 2026-10-08), each a PhysicsNeMo `DomainMesh` directory in dimensional
SI units with the applied pose, read natively by the recipe.** No
conversion step exists for this dataset: the release is already in the
recipe's mesh format.

- **Layout.** `shard-NNN/<case_id>/domain.pdmsh`. The interior is a point
  cloud of cell centroids with the seven solution fields and the cell
  volumes as `point_data`; the four boundaries are triangle meshes with
  all data on the cells: the solution fields on every boundary, the
  prescribed values under `prescribed.dirichlet.*` (the inlet velocity and
  its four turbulence quantities, the outlet gauge pressure, the wall
  velocity) and the outlet's reverse-flow fallbacks under
  `prescribed.reverse_flow.*`. The global data hold the fluid (density,
  kinematic viscosity), the reference velocity, speed, length and dynamic
  pressure, and identity and diagnostic blocks that are never inputs. Face
  counts run from 23 to 1.8 million per boundary type; a case without slip
  walls has a slip mesh of zero faces.
- **The row-permuted copy.** The release stores interior points in the
  solver's cell order, which is spatially coherent: a contiguous block of
  200,000 rows covers 8 to 42 percent of the domain's bounding box. The
  recipe's reader draws its interior subsample as one contiguous block,
  so training and scoring read a derived copy in which every interior's
  rows are randomly permuted once (seeded by the case id; after the
  permutation a block covers 97 to 99 percent of the box); boundaries and
  global data are the release's own files, so the boundary faces keep the
  solver's order (@sec-interior-aerozoo gives what that does to the
  results).
- **Normalization** (`aerozoo_volume.yaml`). Coordinates are divided by
  the reference length and centered on the interior sample's mean.
  Velocity is divided by the reference speed, the gauge pressure by the
  reference dynamic pressure (so `pressure` is a pressure coefficient),
  the turbulent viscosity by speed times length, the turbulent kinetic
  energy by the speed squared and the specific dissipation rate by speed
  over length; the same rules apply to the prescribed values on the
  boundaries. The Reynolds number enters as $(\log_{10}(U L / \nu) -
  5.5) / 1.5$. Each target is then standardized by its mean and standard
  deviation over the training side of the split in use (a seeded
  20,000-point sample of every training case), so the per-field relative
  L2 is computed on the standardized field: its ratios between models are
  orderings under that centering, not physical percentages, as for eddy
  viscosity on AirfRANS (@sec-airfrans-measured).
- **The specific-dissipation tail.** The standardized specific
  dissipation rate has a heavy tail that the other fields do not: of the
  3,815 cases, 238 carry at least one interior point above 1,000 standard
  deviations, 110 above 10,000 and three above ten million, each a single
  point whose rate is ten to twelve orders of magnitude above the field's
  mean while the case's other fields are ordinary. Two consequences
  follow. In training, a sampled block that holds one of those points
  gives a step loss of 24 to 2,086 against a typical 0.04, identical for
  every architecture because the Huber loss is linear there; these steps
  are isolated and neither model's trajectory turns on them. In scoring,
  the per-case relative L2 of the specific dissipation saturates at 1.0
  whenever one point dominates the target norm, so that column is partly
  a count of such cases rather than a measure of the field, for every
  arm alike. The pressure coefficient of the fastest cases (46 training
  cases with a mean above three standard deviations) and the eddy
  viscosity of the slowest (36, mostly the opposed-hemisphere and
  opposed-sphere enclosures) are the other wide fields. No field is
  clipped or transformed beyond the normalization above.
- **What each model receives.** ISLA: the four boundary meshes with the
  faces' positions, normals and areas, a one-hot of the condition type
  per face and the prescribed values (zero where a type prescribes
  nothing; the velocity as a rank-1 input, the scalars as rank 0), the
  inlet direction as the one global vector, and the standardized log
  Reynolds number and the inlet's four standardized turbulence quantities
  as five global scalars; the interior queries carry no stored field
  (ISLA computes each query's distance and direction to the nearest
  boundary token itself). GeoTransolver: the interior points with their
  coordinates, the signed distance and its gradient to the no-slip
  walls and the signed distance to the slip walls, all computed from the
  same sampled boundary, and a global vector of the inlet direction, the
  log Reynolds number and the four inlet turbulence quantities, the same
  global information. The two wall meshes are not "the body" and "the
  enclosure": a body's slip bands sit on the slip mesh beside the
  symmetry planes, and a ground plane or a duct wall sits on the no-slip
  mesh beside the body, so both distances mix body and enclosure.
  GeoTransolver has no channel at all for the inlet and outlet faces, and
  one case in seven carries a secondary inlet whose prescribed velocity
  reaches ISLA as per-face values and reaches GeoTransolver not at all
  (the global vector holds the primary inlet's direction). Neither model
  sees the body identifier, the solution or derived fields, or the
  diagnostics.
- **Splits.** `full`: 2,713 train / 386 validation / 716 test. The
  held-out splits used here train on everything but one family and test
  on it: `family_non_box` (2,390 / 351 / 1,074: trained on external boxes,
  tested on the hemisphere, sphere and duct enclosures), `reynolds` (2,119
  / 311 / 1,385: trained below $10^6$, tested above) and `bank_blobs`
  (2,156 / 292 / 1,367: the largest bank held out). Model selection uses
  the validation side only; the test side of every split is scored once.
- **Stability populations.** The release labels each case `mean_stable`
  or `mean_unstable` from the solver's block-mean drift of velocity and
  pressure. Both stay in every split; @tbl-aerozoo-quality reports them
  apart.

## What is measured {#sec-aerozoo-measured}

```{python}
#| label: para-aerozoo-measured
#| output: asis
S = SPLITS["full"]
print(f"**The interior task of @sec-interior-task on the `full` split: {S['n_train']:,} training cases, {N_HEAD:,} cases on {SIDE_WORD}, 200,000 interior "
      f"queries and up to 50,000 faces per boundary type per case (one contiguous window of the stored faces, @sec-interior-aerozoo), 250 epochs, {N_SEEDS} seeds, float32.** "
      + " ".join(f"{CONFIG[a]} ({PARAMS[a]:.0f}M parameters)" + (";" if i < len(ARMS) - 1 else ".") for i, a in enumerate(ARMS)) + " "
      "The reference configurations are those the characterization campaign fixed for the DrivAerML Volume task (@sec-protocol); no lane trains "
      "with rotation or translation augmentation, and the epoch count is chosen so the `full` split's training steps match the 1,260-wing rung's "
      "within 8 percent. The metric is the relative L2 per field averaged over the cases, on the standardized fields (@sec-data-aerozoo). The two "
      "architectures do not receive the same inputs: GeoTransolver reads every interior point with its coordinates and three stored distance "
      "quantities computed from the sampled boundary and never sees the boundary faces themselves; ISLA reads the four boundary meshes with their "
      "condition types and prescribed values and computes its own geometry at the queries. The held-out splits train the same configurations "
      "from their own training sides and are scored on the family they hold out.")
rows = [(a, COST[a]) for a in ARMS if COST[a]]
if rows:
    print()
    print("**Cost.** Training on this task, four GB300 ranks in bfloat16, the final epoch's median step time and the peak device memory any rank "
          "reports: " + "; ".join(f"{a} {c['step_s']:.2f} s per step and {c['mem_gb']:.0f} GB at {c['params'] / 1e6:.0f}M parameters"
                                  + (f", about {c['gpu_h']:.0f} GPU-hours for the 250 epochs" if c["gpu_h"] else "") for a, c in rows)
          + f". One epoch of the `full` split is {rows[0][1]['steps_per_epoch']:,} steps at one case per rank. Data: results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/aerozoo_reduction.json (cost).")
```

## The standing in distribution {#sec-interior-aerozoo}

```{python}
#| label: para-aerozoo-standing-lede
#| output: asis
r = {f: rat("GeoTransolver", "full", SIDE, f) for f in FKEYS}
counts = [FLAB[f] for f in FKEYS if r[f]["counts"]]
print(f"**On {SIDE_WORD} of the `full` split GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA reads "
      + ", ".join(f"{fmt_ratio(r[f]['mean_ratio'])} on {FLAB[f]}" for f in FKEYS)
      + (f"; the differences that count under the book's rule (both seeds ordered the same way and the seed-mean ratio outside 1 ± 0.05) are on {', '.join(counts)}" if counts else
         "; none of the differences counts under the book's rule (both seeds ordered the same way and the seed-mean ratio outside 1 ± 0.05)")
      + ".** @tbl-aerozoo-full is the standing; every number below is read from it.")
```

**Every volume result in this chapter was produced with each boundary
mesh above 50,000 faces read as one contiguous window of faces in solver
order, not as a uniform sample of the boundary.** The reader caps each
boundary at 50,000 faces by taking one contiguous block of the stored
faces at a random offset per draw, with the measure scaled by the
boundary's face count over 50,000. The interior rows are permuted
(@sec-data-aerozoo), but the boundary faces keep OpenFOAM's order, which
runs through space, so each draw of a large boundary is one spatially
coherent patch. Two thirds of the cases with a body have more than 50,000
no-slip faces. A draw holds on average 56 percent of the body's faces, and
about a quarter of the draws hold no face of the body at all. The scorer
draws once per case, so about a quarter of the scored cases were
predicted without the body in the input. GeoTransolver's wall distances
are computed from the same windowed boundaries, so both architectures
received the same defective input: the comparisons between them are like
for like, but the task they were compared on was degraded. Lanes that
read each boundary whole and draw 50,000 of its faces uniformly at random,
with the same measure scaling, replace every result of this chapter when
they complete.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-aerozoo-full
#| output: asis
sides = [s for s in ("val", "test") if all(have(a, "full", s) for a in ("ISLA", "GeoTransolver"))]
SIDE_LABEL = {"val": "validation (386 cases)", "test": "test (716 cases, scored once)"}
flab = " / ".join(FLAB[f] for f in FKEYS)
hdr = "| configuration | " + " | ".join(f"{SIDE_LABEL[s]}: {flab}" for s in sides) + " |\n|---|" + "---|" * len(sides) + "\n"
rows = []
for a in ARMS:
    if not all(have(a, "full", s) for s in sides):
        continue
    one = any(blk(a, "full", s)["fields"][f]["n_seeds"] < 2 for s in sides for f in FKEYS)
    rows.append(f"| {CONFIG[a].split(',')[0]}{' (one seed)' if one else ''} | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{err(a, 'full', s, f):.4f}" for f in FKEYS) for s in sides) + " |")
    if a != "ISLA":
        rows.append(f"| {a} ÷ ISLA | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{rat(a, 'full', s, f)['mean_ratio']:.2f}" for f in FKEYS) for s in sides) + " |")
print(hdr + "\n".join(rows) + "\n")
print(f": The AeroZoo interior task at {SPLITS['full']['n_train']:,} training cases: the architectures at their reference configurations, relative L2 per "
      f"field on the standardized fields averaged over the cases of each side, seed means over two seeds unless the row says one, float32, 200,000 "
      f"queries per case, each boundary above 50,000 faces read as one contiguous window of faces (@sec-interior-aerozoo). Fields {flab}. How to read this: a ratio is baseline ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA; the validation side selected "
      "nothing (the protocol has no early stopping) and the test side was scored once; the two columns share each checkpoint and differ only in "
      "the cases. Data: results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/aerozoo_reduction.json. {#tbl-aerozoo-full}")
```

```{python}
#| label: para-aerozoo-reading
#| output: asis
V = json.load(open(RES / "char" / "drivaerml_volume.json")); VA = {arm.split()[0]: d for arm, d in V["arms"].items()}
A = json.load(open(RES / "char" / "airfrans.json")); AA = {arm.split()[0]: d for arm, d in A["arms"].items()}
vrat = lambda f: VA["GeoTransolver"]["native"][f]["mean"] / VA["ISLA"]["native"][f]["mean"]
arat = lambda f: AA["GeoTransolver"]["native"][f]["mean"] / AA["ISLA"]["native"][f]["mean"]
g = lambda f: rat("GeoTransolver", "full", SIDE, f)["mean_ratio"]
paired = lambda f: rat("GeoTransolver", "full", SIDE, f)["per_seed_ratio"]
bar_v = g("velocity_l2") >= 1.2; bar_p = g("pressure_l2") <= 0.9
fals = g("velocity_l2") < 1.1 or g("pressure_l2") > 1.0
pattern = ("holds" if bar_v and bar_p else "fails" if fals else "holds in part")
print(f"Three readings. First, the pattern of the two existing interior datasets, a velocity lead for ISLA and a pressure lead for GeoTransolver "
      f"(GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA {vrat('velocity_l2'):.2f} and {vrat('pressure_l2'):.2f} on the DrivAerML Volume task, {fmt_ratio(arat('velocity_l2'))} and "
      f"{arat('pressure_l2'):.2f} on AirfRANS, whose interior was read as one contiguous window of the stored points; @tbl-drivaerml-volume-protocols, "
      f"@tbl-airfrans-protocols, @sec-interior-airfrans), {pattern} here: velocity "
      f"{fmt_ratio(g('velocity_l2'))} (paired by seed {', '.join(f'{v:.2f}' for v in paired('velocity_l2').values())}) and pressure "
      f"{g('pressure_l2'):.2f} ({', '.join(f'{v:.2f}' for v in paired('pressure_l2').values())}), against the bar written before the lanes ran of at "
      f"least 1.2 on velocity and at most 0.9 on pressure. Second, the three turbulence fields, which no earlier dataset of the book predicts "
      f"together: eddy viscosity {fmt_ratio(g('nut_l2'))}, turbulent kinetic energy {fmt_ratio(g('tke_l2'))} and the specific dissipation rate "
      f"{fmt_ratio(g('omega_l2'))}; the dissipation rate is standardized over a range of four decades (its training-side standard deviation is "
      f"fifteen times its mean), so its relative L2 is dominated by the near-wall cells where $\\omega$ is largest and both models' absolute "
      f"errors there are a property of the field, not of the architecture. Third, what the two models were given: the same global information "
      f"and the same boundary sample, but GeoTransolver through three distances and ISLA through the faces themselves with their condition types "
      f"and prescribed values, so a difference on this dataset is a difference between reading a boundary and reading a distance to it, under the "
      f"same training budget. The enclosure, which GeoTransolver sees only through the two wall distances and the extent of the point cloud "
      f"(its inlet and outlet it does not see at all), is where the two readings should part, and @sec-aerozoo-heldout holds the enclosure "
      f"family out to test that.")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
Q = {a: strata(a, "quality") for a in ARMS if have(a, "full", SIDE) and "by_quality" in blk(a, "full", SIDE)}
pops = [p for p in ("mean_stable", "mean_unstable") if all(p in Q[a] for a in Q)]
hdr = "| configuration | " + " | ".join(f"{p.replace('_', ' ')} ({Q['ISLA'][p]['n_cases']:,} cases): {flab}" for p in pops) + " |\n|---|" + "---|" * len(pops) + "\n"
rows = []
for a in Q:
    rows.append(f"| {CONFIG[a].split(',')[0]} | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{Q[a][p][f]['mean']:.4f}" for f in FKEYS) for p in pops) + " |")
    if a != "ISLA":
        rows.append(f"| {a} ÷ ISLA | " + " | ".join(" / ".join(f"{Q[a][p][f]['mean'] / Q['ISLA'][p][f]['mean']:.2f}" for f in FKEYS) for p in pops) + " |")
print(hdr + "\n".join(rows) + "\n")
print(f": The two stability populations of {SIDE_WORD} of the `full` split, scored apart: the same checkpoints and the same metric as @tbl-aerozoo-full, "
      f"the cases split by the release's convergence label (`mean_stable`: the solver's block means of velocity and pressure settled; "
      f"`mean_unstable`: they still drifted, so the time-averaged labels carry solver noise). Fields {flab}; seed means, float32. How to read this: "
      "a ratio is GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA, above one favoring ISLA; the unstable population's absolute errors include the labels' own noise, so only "
      "the ratios are comparable across the two columns. Data: results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/aerozoo_reduction.json (by_quality). {#tbl-aerozoo-quality}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-aerozoo-strata
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Error by family on the test side of the `full` split: interior velocity
#|   (left) and pressure (right) relative L2, the test cases split by the
#|   enclosure (top), the geometry bank (middle) and the decade of Reynolds
#|   number (bottom), for the architectures at their reference configurations;
#|   the mark is the seed mean, the short ticks the two seeds, and the case
#|   count of each family is printed under its name. How to read this: the
#|   families are categories, so no line joins them except across the ordered
#|   Reynolds decades; every family here was seen in training (this is the
#|   in-distribution split), so the spread across families is the task's
#|   difficulty, not generalization; the metric is on the standardized field.
#|   Data: results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/aerozoo_reduction.json (by_label).
#| code-fold: true
KINDS = [("enclosure", "enclosure"), ("bank", "geometry bank"), ("log10_re_decade", "Reynolds-number decade")]
NICE = {"rectangular_prism": "external\nbox", "opposed_hemisphere": "opposed\nhemispheres", "opposed_sphere": "opposed\nspheres", "internal_duct": "internal\nduct",
        "blender_streamlined": "Blender streamlined", "blender_bluff": "Blender bluff", "zero_to_cad": "CAD bank", "streamlined": "streamlined", "cars": "cars",
        "airframes": "airframes", "blobs": "blobs"}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(10.5, 9.6), gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.55, wspace=0.22))
for row, (kind, klab) in enumerate(KINDS):
    S0 = strata("ISLA", kind)
    cats = [c for c in S0 if c not in ("unlabeled", "None") and S0[c]["n_cases"] >= 5]
    cats = sorted(cats, key=(lambda c: int(c[2:])) if kind == "log10_re_decade" else (lambda c: -S0[c]["n_cases"]))
    for col, f in enumerate(("velocity_l2", "pressure_l2")):
        ax = axes[row, col]; xs = np.arange(len(cats))
        for a in ARMS:
            if not have(a, "full", SIDE) or "by_label" not in blk(a, "full", SIDE):
                continue
            Sa = strata(a, kind); kw = series_kwargs(KEY[a])
            ys = [Sa[c][f]["mean"] if c in Sa and f in Sa[c] else np.nan for c in cats]
            ax.plot(xs, ys, marker=kw["marker"], color=kw["color"], mfc=kw["mfc"], mec=kw["mec"], mew=kw["mew"], ms=7, lw=(1.4 if kind == "log10_re_decade" else 0), ls=(kw["ls"] if kind == "log10_re_decade" else "none"), label=kw["label"], zorder=5)
            for x, c in zip(xs, cats):
                if c in Sa and f in Sa[c]:
                    seed_marks(ax, x, Sa[c][f]["per_seed"].values(), kw["color"])
        many = len(cats) > 5
        ax.set_xticks(xs)
        ax.set_xticklabels([f"{NICE.get(c, c)} ({S0[c]['n_cases']:,})" if many else f"{NICE.get(c, c)}\n({S0[c]['n_cases']:,})" for c in cats],
                           fontsize=7.8, rotation=(28 if many else 0), ha=("right" if many else "center"), rotation_mode="anchor")
        ax.set_xlim(-0.6, len(cats) - 0.4)
        ax.set_ylim(0, None); ax.set_ylabel(f"{FLAB[f]} relative L2 [–]")
        ax.set_title(f"by {klab}: {FLAB[f]}", fontsize=9.5)
handles = [Line2D([], [], marker=STYLE[KEY[a]]["marker"], color=STYLE[KEY[a]]["color"], mfc=(STYLE[KEY[a]]["color"] if STYLE[KEY[a]]["mfc"] == "full" else "white"),
                  ls="none", ms=7, mew=1.8, label=STYLE[KEY[a]]["label"]) for a in ARMS]
fig.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower center", ncol=len(ARMS), fontsize=8.5, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.005))
plt.show()
```

```{python}
               "mixed": f"the bar written before the lanes ran (ISLA's penalty at least 20 percent smaller than GeoTransolver's) holds on {P2.get('n_supported', 0)} of {P2.get('n_fields', 0)} fields and fails on {P2.get('n_falsified', 0)}",
               "between": "ISLA's penalty is smaller than GeoTransolver's but by less than the 20 percent the bar written before the lanes ran asked for"}.get(P2.get("verdict"), "")
    heldbv = ""
    bi = BVR.get("ISLA", {}).get("family_non_box", {}).get("test"); bg = BVR.get("GeoTransolver", {}).get("family_non_box", {}).get("test")
    if bi and bg and "family_non_box" in HELD:
        rbb = {f: bg["fields"][f]["mean"] / bi["fields"][f]["mean"] for f in FKEYS}
        gt_leads = [f for f in FKEYS if rbb[f] < 1]
        heldbv = ("The enclosure reading is not an artifact of ISLA's post-event checkpoints: at both architectures' best-validation checkpoints "
                  "(@tbl-aerozoo-bestckpt) GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA on the held-out enclosures is " + " / ".join(f"{rbb[f]:.2f}" for f in FKEYS)
                  + (", GeoTransolver ahead on every field. " if len(gt_leads) == len(FKEYS) else f", GeoTransolver ahead on {len(gt_leads)} of the five fields. "))
    print("**" + "; ".join(parts) + (f". For the enclosure, {verdict}" if verdict and "family_non_box" in HELD else "") + ".** " + heldbv +
          "Each held-out split trains the same configurations from its own training side (every case outside the family) and is scored on the "
          "family it holds out; a penalty is that error divided by the same architecture's error on the `full` test side, so it is a "
          "within-configuration readout, and the ratio of the two architectures' penalties is the comparison. @tbl-aerozoo-heldout holds the numbers "
          "and @fig-aerozoo-penalties draws them. The held-out lanes read each boundary as one contiguous window of faces, as the `full` lanes do "
          "(@sec-interior-aerozoo).")
```

```{python}
          f"means, float32. Fields {flab}. A penalty divides the held-out test error by the same architecture's error on the `full` test side "

          "read this: the held-out splits train on 2,100 to 2,400 cases against the `full` split's 2,713, so part of every penalty is data size and both "
```

```{python}
                   f"{', '.join(more) if more else 'no field'} (both seeds agreeing, ratio of penalties outside 1 ± 0.05); on the held-out family itself "
                   f"GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is {fmt_ratio(vg / vi)} on velocity and {fmt_ratio(err('GeoTransolver', s, 'test', 'pressure_l2') / err('ISLA', s, 'test', 'pressure_l2'))} on pressure.")
    print(" ".join(txt) + " The mechanism the enclosure split was built to test is that ISLA reads the far boundary as faces with their condition types "
          "where GeoTransolver reads it through one distance and the extent of the point cloud; the numbers above are the measurement, and the routing "
          "and territory probes that would show how each model represents an unseen enclosure have not been run on these lanes.")
```

## Training trajectories {#sec-aerozoo-trajectories}

```{python}
#| label: para-aerozoo-trajectories
#| output: asis
TR = R["trajectories"]; RUNS = R["runs"]
# the detector is the reduction's: the first validation epoch whose loss exceeds twice the running minimum before it
ev = {run: EV[run]["event_epoch"] for run in TR if RUNS[run]["split"] == "full" and EV.get(run) and RUNS[run]["arm"] in ARMS}
by_arm = {}
for run, e in ev.items():
    by_arm.setdefault(RUNS[run]["arm"], []).append((RUNS[run]["seed"], e, EV[run]["best_epoch"]))
hit = {a: [x for x in v if x[1] is not None] for a, v in by_arm.items()}
isla_hits = sorted(hit.get("ISLA", [])); gt_hits = hit.get("GeoTransolver", [])
BV = BVR.get("ISLA", {}).get("full", {}).get("val"); FV = blk("ISLA", "full", "val") if have("ISLA", "full", "val") else None
if isla_hits:
    print(f"**Every ISLA lane on this split reaches its validation-loss minimum early (epochs {', '.join(str(x[2]) for x in isla_hits)} for "
          f"seeds {', '.join(str(x[0]) for x in isla_hits)}) and then loses it: at epochs {', '.join(str(x[1]) for x in isla_hits)} the validation "
          f"loss doubles its running minimum and stays two- to four-fold above it to epoch 250"
          + (", while no GeoTransolver lane shows the event" if not gt_hits else f", and GeoTransolver seeds {', '.join(str(x[0]) for x in gt_hits)} show it at epochs {', '.join(str(x[1]) for x in gt_hits)}")
          + ".** The training loss rises with the validation loss, so the event sits in the optimization and not in the fit. It is not the "
          "mean-field plateau of the DeepJEB++ lanes (@sec-deepjeb): the routing narrows but keeps more than thirty effective slices in every block, "
          "no weight tensor moves out of line with the others, the weights' motion slows to a third of its earlier rate, the tenfold rate step at "
          "epoch 100 does not bring the loss back, and the degradation is uniform over the validation cases, every bank and enclosure alike "
          "(`results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/probe/routing_*.json` and `drift_*.json`). The same event ends every ISLA lane of the "
          "campaign, on every split, between epochs 43 and 50 for the dense read and 54 and 65 for the tree read. ")
    if BV and FV:
        ep = ", ".join(f"epoch {e} for seed {s}" for s, e in BV["epochs"].items())
        print(f"Scored exactly like the protocol on the validation side, ISLA's best-validation checkpoint ({ep}) reads "
              + " / ".join(f"{BV['fields'][f]['mean']:.3f}" for f in FKEYS) + f" on {flab}, against the final checkpoints' "
              + " / ".join(f"{FV['fields'][f]['mean']:.3f}" for f in FKEYS) + "; the standing of @tbl-aerozoo-full is the final checkpoint by the "
              "protocol, and the best-checkpoint numbers are a labeled diagnostic of what the architecture had learned before the event "
              "(@tbl-aerozoo-bestckpt gives them for every arm and both sides). ")
        bit = BVR.get("ISLA", {}).get("full", {}).get("test"); bgt = BVR.get("GeoTransolver", {}).get("full", {}).get("test")
        if bit and bgt:
            rr = {f: bgt["fields"][f]["mean"] / bit["fields"][f]["mean"] for f in FKEYS}
            print("Best checkpoint against best checkpoint on the sealed test side, GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA reads " + " / ".join(f"{rr[f]:.2f}" for f in FKEYS)
                  + (": before the event ISLA leads on every field, " if all(v > 1 for v in rr.values()) else ", ")
                  + "so the in-distribution standing of @tbl-aerozoo-full belongs to the training protocol and not to the architecture; the held-out "
                  "standing does not move the same way (@sec-aerozoo-heldout). ")
else:
    last = {run: max(r["epoch"] for r in rows) for run, rows in TR.items() if rows and RUNS[run]["split"] == "full"}
    print(f"**No `full`-split lane shows a validation loss that doubles its running minimum: every validation loss keeps falling or holds to its "
          f"last validation (epochs {min(last.values())} to {max(last.values())}).** ")
# the rate control: the half-rate arms where they have trained, read against their reference-rate twins (reduction: remedy)
for a in HR_ARMS:
    m = R.get("remedy", {}).get(a)
    if not m:
        continue
    lanes = m["lanes"]; twin = m["twin"]
    far = min(l["last_epoch"] for l in lanes.values()); furthest = max(l["last_epoch"] for l in lanes.values())
    where = ", ".join(f"`{SPLITS[sp]['stem']}` seed {l['seed']}" for sp in ("full", "family_non_box") for l in lanes.values() if l["split"] == sp)
    hits = {r: l for r, l in lanes.items() if l["event_epoch"] is not None}
    if hits:
        print(f"**At half the reference rate ({CONFIG[a]}; lanes {where}) the event {'recurs' if m['code'] == 'R3' else 'comes later'}: the validation "
              f"loss doubles its running minimum at epochs {', '.join(str(l['event_epoch']) for l in hits.values())} against "
              f"{', '.join(str(e['event_epoch']) for e in m['twin_events'].values() if e['event_epoch'] is not None)} for {twin} at the reference rate.** "
              + ("The cause is therefore not the step count at this rate, and the half rate does not help this dataset. "
                 if m["code"] == "R3" else "The event is rate-bound in the way the DeepJEB++ one is (@sec-deepjeb). "))
    else:
        fv = m.get("full_val_velocity")
        print(f"**At half the reference rate ({CONFIG[a]}; lanes {where}) no lane doubles its running validation minimum through epoch {far}"
              + (f" (the furthest lane through epoch {furthest})" if furthest > far else "")
              + f", where {twin} at the reference rate doubled at epochs {', '.join(str(e['event_epoch']) for e in m['twin_events'].values() if e['event_epoch'] is not None)}"
              + (f", and the final `full` checkpoints read velocity {fv:.3f} on the validation side" if fv is not None else "") + ".** "
              + ("With the raw slice reads, the half rate cures the event on this dataset" + (f"; GeoTransolver ÷ {a} on test velocity reads {m['p1_reread']['velocity_ratio']:.2f} against the pre-registered 1.4. "
                 if m["p1_reread"]["velocity_ratio"] is not None else ". ") if m["code"] == "R2" else ""))
print("@fig-aerozoo-trajectories draws the validation loss and the interior velocity error of every `full`-split lane against the epoch, the trainer's "
      "own validation every ten epochs in bfloat16 on the 386 validation cases at the training draw; the float32 standings of @tbl-aerozoo-full are "
      "scored from the final checkpoints. Data: results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/aerozoo_reduction.json (trajectories, events, remedy, bestval).")
```

```{python}
    print()

          "exactly like @tbl-aerozoo-full: float32, 200,000 points per case, relative L2 of the standardized field, seed mean. Each cell is the best "
          "checkpoint's error with the final checkpoint's standing on the same side in parentheses; a dash in the epoch column is a seed not scored "
          "on that side. How to read this: the selection uses the validation side, so the validation rows are optimistic by construction and the test "
          "rows are the fair reading of what each architecture had learned under the reference protocol before its training protocol failed it, if "
          "it failed. Data: results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/aerozoo_reduction.json (bestval). {#tbl-aerozoo-bestckpt}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-aerozoo-trajectories
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Validation trajectories of the `full`-split lanes: the trainer's validation
#|   loss (top; the Huber loss summed over the five standardized targets) and
#|   the interior velocity relative L2 (bottom) every ten epochs, bfloat16, on
#|   the 386 validation cases at the training draw. The line is the two seeds'
#|   mean and the band spans the seeds; ISLA in blue, GeoTransolver in red,
#|   ISLA-DTT in light blue where it ran. How to read this: the step in the
#|   ISLA curves between epochs 40 and 60 is the optimization event of
#|   @sec-aerozoo-trajectories, a three- to fourfold rise that the rest of the
#|   run never recovers, and not the routing collapse of the DeepJEB++ chapter,
#|   which would send velocity to about one; the final standings of
#|   @tbl-aerozoo-full are float32 scorings of the last checkpoints and sit a
#|   few percent below these bfloat16 validations; the axis is logarithmic.
#|   Dashed and dotted blue lines are the half-rate lanes (1.875e-4) where they
#|   have trained. Data:
#|   results/campaigns_2026-10-09/aerozoo/aerozoo_reduction.json (trajectories).
#| code-fold: true
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 6.4), sharex=True, gridspec_kw=dict(hspace=0.12))
for a in ARMS + HR_ARMS:
    runs = [r for r, m in RUNS.items() if m["arm"] == a and m["split"] == "full" and TR.get(r)]
    if not runs:
        continue
    kw = series_kwargs(KEY[a])
    for ax, key in zip(axes, ("loss", "velocity_l2")):
        by_epoch = {}
        for r in runs:
            for row in TR[r]:
                if row.get(key) is not None:
                    by_epoch.setdefault(row["epoch"], []).append(row[key])
        ep = sorted(by_epoch); m = [mean(by_epoch[e]) for e in ep]; lo = [min(by_epoch[e]) for e in ep]; hi = [max(by_epoch[e]) for e in ep]
        ax.plot(ep, m, color=kw["color"], ls=kw["ls"], lw=1.8, label=kw["label"])
        ax.fill_between(ep, lo, hi, color=kw["color"], alpha=0.18, lw=0)
plain = mpl.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:g}")
for ax, lab in zip(axes, ("validation loss [–]", "interior velocity relative L2 [–]")):
    ax.set_yscale("log"); ax.set_ylabel(lab)
    lo, hi = ax.get_ylim(); ticks = [t for t in (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2) if lo <= t <= hi]
    ax.set_yticks(ticks); ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plain); ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper right"); axes[1].set_xlabel("epoch [count]")
plt.show()
```

## Ladders and controls {#sec-aerozoo-ladders}

```{python}
#| label: para-aerozoo-controls
#| output: asis
if "ISLA-DTT" in ARMS and have("ISLA-DTT", "full", SIDE):
    rs = {f: rat("ISLA-DTT", "full", SIDE, f) for f in FKEYS}
    dev = max(abs(rs[f]["mean_ratio"] - 1) for f in FKEYS)
    print(f"**The one control on this dataset is ISLA-DTT, the reference configuration with the tree-accelerated query-independent read in place of the "
          f"dense one: on {SIDE_WORD} of the `full` split it reads " + ", ".join(f"{rs[f]['mean_ratio']:.3f} of ISLA on {FLAB[f]}" for f in FKEYS)
          + f", a largest deviation of {dev * 100:.1f}% against the bar of 5% written before the lanes ran, which it {'meets' if dev <= 0.05 else 'fails'}.** "
          "No width, depth or cell-count control was run on this dataset, and the one rate control is the half-rate lanes of @sec-aerozoo-trajectories; "
          "the reference configurations are those the characterization campaign fixed on the DrivAerML Volume task and were not re-selected here.")
else:
    print("**No control lane beyond the reference configurations has been scored on this dataset: the reference configurations are those the "
          "characterization campaign fixed on the DrivAerML Volume task and were not re-selected here, and no width, depth, rate or cell-count control was run.** "
          "The ISLA-DTT lanes, the reference configuration with the tree-accelerated query-independent read, are the one planned control, with a bar of 5% on every field.")
```

## What this dataset does not say {#sec-aerozoo-limits}

```{python}
#| label: para-aerozoo-limits
#| output: asis
print(f"**The AeroZoo standing is one dataset and one task, the interior fields from the boundaries alone, scored on the standardized fields: a "
      f"velocity ratio of {fmt_ratio(rat('GeoTransolver', 'full', SIDE, 'velocity_l2')['mean_ratio'])}, a pressure ratio of "
      f"{rat('GeoTransolver', 'full', SIDE, 'pressure_l2')['mean_ratio']:.2f}, three turbulence fields, {'the held-out penalties of @tbl-aerozoo-heldout' if HELD else 'and the held-out splits still to be scored'}.** "
      "Every number here was produced with each boundary above 50,000 faces read as one contiguous window of faces, so that about a quarter of the "
      "draws held no face of the body, for both architectures alike (@sec-interior-aerozoo): the ratios compare like for like on a degraded task, "
      "and the uniform-sampling lanes replace them when they complete. "
      "The two configurations are not resource-matched and do not receive the same inputs (@sec-aerozoo-measured), so the ratios are standings of the "
      "configurations as shipped, and every ISLA number is the checkpoint after the optimization event of @sec-aerozoo-trajectories under the "
      "reference training protocol, which the protocol scores as it stands; what the architecture reaches under a protocol that survives this "
      f"dataset is measured only as the labeled best-checkpoint diagnostic of @tbl-aerozoo-bestckpt (the `{'`, `'.join(sorted({sp for a in BVR for sp in BVR[a]}, key=lambda x: (x != 'full', x)))}` "
      f"split{'s' if len({sp for a in BVR for sp in BVR[a]}) > 1 else ''}, {' and '.join(sorted({ {'test': 'the test', 'val': 'the validation'}[sd] for a in BVR for sp in BVR[a] for sd in BVR[a][sp]}, reverse=True))} side"
      f"{'s' if len({sd for a in BVR for sp in BVR[a] for sd in BVR[a][sp]}) > 1 else ''})"
      + (" and by the half-rate arms where they have trained (@sec-aerozoo-trajectories)" if HR_ARMS else "") + ", not on the Reynolds and blob-bank splits. "
      "The surface task on this dataset, the boundary solution fields and the wall shear from the same inputs, is not "
      "measured. The uniform-point-cloud and rotated-and-translated scorings of the other chapters were not run here: the interior is already a point "
      "cloud, and the pose contract is measured on the surface datasets (@sec-invariances). The held-out penalties mix generalization with data size "
      "(every held-out split trains on fewer cases than `full`), which is why only their ratio across architectures is read, and the mechanism behind "
      "a smaller or larger penalty is not measured on these lanes. A quarter of the labels are time averages the solver marked as still drifting; "
      "@tbl-aerozoo-quality shows the standing does not depend on them, and nothing here says how large that label noise is in physical units.")
```
